canvas-01.description: The lower half of printed sheet 1 is a large-scale map, at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, of the industrial block south of the Central Railroad of New Jersey between Church Street and Clinton Street, with Atlantic along the top edge and Water (Bank) Street near the bottom. West of Church Street stands the Wickham Co. of New Jersey works, manufacturers of piano plates: a long foundry, a finishing shop with ovens and drilling rooms, a machine shop, sand blast and chipping rooms, with watchman, hose cart and hydrant notes. East of Church Street is A. P. Munning and Co., manufacturers of electro-plating and buffing apparatus and supplies, with its composition building, foundry, soap house, rouge building, furnace building, R. E. annex and main factory building beside a railroad platform. In the lower left corner the Matawan Water Works pumping station draws from three artesian wells, with its settling reservoirs and clear water reservoir. A few frame dwellings stand along Water Street and on the east side of the block. The upper half of the sheet, with the title, key, index and a key map of the town at 900 feet to an inch, is not part of this annotation.
notes: Atlantic is today Atlantic Street.
Placed by a helmert fit through two points about 215 m apart (Atlantic Street / Clinton Street detected from one drawn edge, Church Street / Water Street hand-picked): low confidence.
The heavy line across the middle of the sheet divides this map from the key map above; only the lower half is georeferenced.

Printed sheet 1. Upper half: title, key, index and a key map of the town at 900 ft to an inch (not georeferenced). Lower half: large-scale map at 50 ft to an inch of the Wickham Co. piano plate works and A. P. Munning & Co. plating works between the C.R.R. of N.J., Church Street, Water (Bank) Street and Clinton Street; configured as canvas-01 (one part, the key map left out). North toward the upper right.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the western outskirts of Matawan at 100 feet to an inch, north toward the upper right. Main Street runs diagonally from Schenck Avenue at the right edge, where sheet 3 continues it, down to the Central Railroad of New Jersey at Freneau Station, drawn as a small depot in the lower left corner. Old Bridge Road leaves Main Street toward the north-west and forks with Amboy Road, which runs south to the railroad. Most of the sheet is large undivided tracts with a few frame dwellings and outbuildings along Main Street, Old Bridge Road and Amboy Road, a small group of attached dwellings at the Old Bridge Road corner, and a brook along the top of the sheet. At the upper right the ends of Schenck Avenue, Monroe and Center are drawn. A water pipe runs along Main Street with hydrants. The sheet is sparsely built and shows the edge of the town in 1923.
notes: Old Bridge Rd is today New Brunswick Avenue; Amboy Rd is today Sutphin Avenue (the junction lies about 230 m west of Main Street on both).
Placed from two detected junctions and one hand-picked one (the Old Bridge Rd / Amboy Rd fork): an exact fit through three points.
Sheet 2, 100 ft. West end: Main Street from Schenck Av. to the C.R.R. of N.J. at Freneau Station; Old Bridge Rd (now New Brunswick Avenue), Amboy Rd (now Sutphin Avenue). Sparse; few junctions.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the western part of Matawan's Main Street at 100 feet to an inch, north toward the upper right. Main Street crosses the sheet from Schenck Avenue on the west to Church Street on the east, where sheet 4 takes over. North of Main lie Jackson Street, Monroe Street and Franklin Street, crossed by Washington Street and by Middlesex, the road to the north, with a small grid of narrow lots between Middlesex and Schenck Avenue reached by an alley and by Center. The Dunlup and Lisk Pottery Company works stands at Washington and Jackson, the Midway Hose Company fire house on Jackson Street, and a deep wooded gulch with its top of bank marked runs north from Main Street toward Wyckoff Street, with the Baptist Church near its mouth. South of Main the sheet is open land: Holmdel Road leads south past a few dwellings and a lumber shed, Bailey Lane ends in the fields, and the large block between South Street and Church Street holds the high school and the public school on Broad Street. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the bottom of the sheet; below it, in the corner, the Wickham piano plate works appears in outline, drawn in full on sheet 1. Frame dwellings predominate, with house numbers along Main Street and water pipes and hydrants marked.
notes: Middlesex (north of Main) and Holmdel Rd (south of Main) are today NJ 34.
Broad Street today continues west across the open block south of Main to NJ 34 on a new line; that junction is not drawn and was excluded.
Dunlup & Lisk Pottery Co. at Washington and Jackson.

Sheet 3, 100 ft. Main Street from Schenck Av. to Church St; Middlesex (now NJ 34), Holmdel Rd (NJ 34 south of Main), Monroe, Jackson, Franklin, Washington, South, Broad, Bailey Lane; Dunlup & Lisk Pottery, high school. Factory corner at bottom right belongs to sheet 1.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the centre of Matawan, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. It runs from Church Street on the west to Little Street and Maiden Lane on the east, and from Wyckoff Street and the bend of Matawan Creek at the top to the Central Railroad of New Jersey and Matawan Lake at the bottom. The main business street is Main Street, lined between Summit Street and Little Street with brick and frame stores, the bank, the post office, the free public library, the fire department house on Jackson Street, the First Methodist Episcopal Church and, near Church Street, the First Presbyterian Church. Behind the stores lie Jackson Street, Fountain Avenue, Morristown Road, Spring Street and Arrowsmith Alley, with frame dwellings on long narrow lots. South of Main Street, Broad Street, Orchard Street and Atlantic Street run parallel through a residential district crossed by Center Street, Park Avenue, New Street, Clinton Street and Division Street; the Second Baptist Church stands on Orchard Street and a proposed standpipe site is marked at Church and Orchard. The bottom of the sheet shows the railroad crossing the lake, its shore and a few dwellings near Water Street, an area drawn in more detail on sheet 1. Water pipes with their sizes and hydrants are marked along the streets, and lot and house numbers are given throughout. The sheet joins sheet 3 along Church Street and sheet 5 along Little Street.
notes: Morristown Rd is today Ravine Drive.
New, south of Broad, is today part of Park Avenue.
Atlantic, between Church and Clinton, is today Atlantic Street.
Fountain is lettered Fountain Av. north of Jackson and Fountain St. between Jackson and Main; today Fountain Avenue ends at Jackson Street.
The modern Center Street junctions with Main and Broad lie 9 to 13 m from the drawn ones and were left out of the fit; Main Street / Park Avenue (6 m) too.

Sheet 4, 100 ft. Downtown: Main, Broad, Jackson, Wyckoff, Orchard between Church and Little; Morristown Rd (now Ravine Drive), New St (now Park Avenue south of Broad), Atlantic (now Atlantic Street). Pilot sheet.

sheet-5-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 5 covers Main Street east of Little Street, north of Matawan Lake, at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Main Street runs across the part from Little Street to the bridge at the head of the lake and on toward Meadow Road; Mill Street, North Street, Cartan Lane and Rabbit Lane (Hill Alley) form a small grid north of it, and Lower Broad runs parallel below it along the lake shore. Matawan Creek winds along the top of the sheet. The west end, at Little Street and Maiden Lane, is the eastern end of the business district, with stores, the Matawan Hotel, a theatre, a private garage, the fire department and the Washington Engine Company house. The Cartan and Devlin lumber and coal yard, with its lumber sheds, fills the block between Mill Street and the creek, and the Episcopal Church stands on Main Street near North Street. The rest of the part is frame dwellings on long lots reaching down to the lake, with house numbers along Main Street and Lower Broad. The southern edge of the part is the middle of the lake; the land beyond it is part 2. Water pipes with their sizes, including a proposed pipe on Lower Broad, and hydrants are marked.
notes: Lower Broad is today part of Broad Street.
The sheet was split into two parts at Matawan Lake: the junctions south of the lake disagree with those north of it by 3 to 8 m in one fit (the lake appears drawn out of scale).
Maiden Lane / Main Street was rejected by the fit (6.9 m).

Sheet 5, 100 ft. Main Street from Little St to Meadow Road, Mill, North, Cartan Lane, Rabbit Lane, Lower Broad (now Broad Street); Matawan Lake; south of the lake Little, Johnson Av., Atlantic Av., Cedar Lane, Mosaic Tile Co. plant no. 2. Two parts: sheet-5-1 north of the lake, sheet-5-2 south and east of it (split at the lake centre: in one fit the two sides disagreed by 3 to 8 m).

sheet-5-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 5 covers the land south and east of Matawan Lake at 100 feet to an inch, north toward the upper right. Little Street crosses the lake on a causeway at the left and runs south-east to Atlantic Avenue, with Johnson Avenue branching south toward the Central Railroad of New Jersey, which crosses the bottom of the sheet with a road bridge. Atlantic Avenue runs along the railroad from Little Street to the east edge, lined on its north side with frame dwellings and with the St. James A. M. E. Zion Church; Cedar Lane leads north from it into large lots running down to the lake. Between Atlantic Avenue and the railroad stand the Frank Anderson basket factory and lumber yard, with three lumber sheds and a locomotive house on the siding, and The Mosaic Tile Co. plant no. 2 with its kilns. In the upper right corner, beyond the lake, Johnson Avenue and Hoyt Street begin, with a wood working factory, continued on sheet 6. A few dwellings stand south of the railroad at the bottom of the sheet. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along Little Street and Atlantic Avenue.
notes: Placed from few junctions south of the lake (Little, Johnson, Atlantic and Hoyt); low confidence.
Modern Johnson Avenue meets Little Street at two nodes about 50 m apart; the sheet draws one junction, and the eastern node was excluded.

Sheet 5, 100 ft. Main Street from Little St to Meadow Road, Mill, North, Cartan Lane, Rabbit Lane, Lower Broad (now Broad Street); Matawan Lake; south of the lake Little, Johnson Av., Atlantic Av., Cedar Lane, Mosaic Tile Co. plant no. 2. Two parts: sheet-5-1 north of the lake, sheet-5-2 south and east of it (split at the lake centre: in one fit the two sides disagreed by 3 to 8 m).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the eastern end of Matawan around the railroad station, at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The Central Railroad of New Jersey and the New York and Long Branch Railroad cross the sheet from top to bottom in a broad band of tracks, with the freight depot, passenger station and Standard Oil Company storage. Main Street crosses the tracks in the middle of the sheet. West of the railroad lie High Street, Division, Bank Street, Short and Canal, with the Aberdeen Inn, a livery, the Thomas H. Hutchison plumbers' supplies warehouse on Johnson Avenue and dwellings on Meadow Road and Aberdeen Road; Matawan Lake reaches the left edge. East of the railroad the Matawan Tile Co. works with its kilns fills the block between the tracks and Water Street, and Cedar Street, Ellis Dock Road and the J. Fischer Co. bag warehouse and Judson Conover grate works lead toward Matawan Creek, which loops across the top of the sheet. Atlantic Avenue runs south-west from Main Street past the Woodbine Hotel toward Hoyt Street, with frame dwellings; 1st Street leads south to the M. L. Erdmann colour works, and Syndam and Davis, an arbitrary name, are laid out on the east edge with a few dwellings. The southern half is mostly open land crossed by the curving branch track.
notes: Main east of the railroad is today Lower Main Street.
Ellis Dock Rd is today Dock Street; Syndam is today Suydam Place; Davis (arbitrary) is today Mathiasen Place; 1st St. is today Harrison Avenue.
Johnson Avenue was left out of the fit: its junction with Hoyt lies 5 to 6 m from the drawn one on both sheet 5 and sheet 6.
The drawn railroad lies about 9 to 14 m from the modern North Jersey Coast Line against the streets; rail crossings were not used.

Sheet 6, 100 ft. Station area east end: Main (Lower Main Street east of the railroad), High, Bank, Division, Short, Water, Cedar, Ellis Dock Rd (now Dock Street), Syndam (now Suydam Place), Davis, 1st St, Johnson Av., Atlantic Av., Hoyt; C.R.R. of N.J. and N.Y. & L.B. R.R.; Matawan Tile Co.
